pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a quote in news? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. The exact words of a person
   C. A map
   D. A price

2. Which is NOT a feeling shown by interjections? (1 mark)
   A. Pain
   B. The price of an item
   C. Joy
   D. Disgust

3. What should you do when someone else is speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Talk over them
   B. Listen without interrupting
   C. Draw
   D. Leave

4. What does rhyme mean? (1 mark)
   A. Words with the same ending sound
   B. Words with capital letters
   C. Words with no vowels
   D. Words with many letters

5. What are images in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Words that make pictures in the mind
   B. Diagrams
   C. Maps
   D. Photographs

6. Why should you mark pauses in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. To hide words
   B. To know where to stop and breathe
   C. To make it longer
   D. To spoil the page

7. How can flashcards help with vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. They make words disappear
   B. They replace reading
   C. They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   D. They cost a lot

8. A good dialogue should have (1 mark)
   A. no words
   B. only one word
   C. an ending
   D. no characters

9. Why should you look back at the dialogue when answering questions? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the page
   B. To waste time
   C. To copy a friend
   D. To find accurate answers

10. What is a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. The order in which things happen
   B. A group of animals
   C. A type of word
   D. A kind of poem

11. What should you do when a stranger offers you a lift? (1 mark)
   A. Go with them
   B. Say no politely and tell a trusted adult
   C. Accept sweets
   D. Give your name

12. Which field asks how old you are? (1 mark)
   A. Class
   B. Signature
   C. Age
   D. School

13. What does reading for information mean? (1 mark)
   A. Reading to learn something new
   B. Reading only for fun
   C. Reading the page numbers
   D. Reading without understanding

14. What is animal welfare? (1 mark)
   A. Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   B. Ignoring animals
   C. Selling animals only
   D. Hunting animals

15. A comma is used to (1 mark)
   A. show a question
   B. begin a sentence
   C. separate items in a list
   D. end a story

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write the verbs in this instruction: Open your book and read page ten. (2 marks)

17. Write two compound sentences about shopping using so and but. (4 marks)

18. Explain why you should not share personal details on a form without asking an adult. (3 marks)

19. Give two reasons why neat handwriting matters. (2 marks)

20. Give two adjectives to describe a school bag in an advert. (2 marks)

21. Name two elements of a story. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — The exact words of a person
   A quote repeats what someone said.

2. B — The price of an item
   Interjections show feelings, not prices.

3. B — Listen without interrupting
   Respectful listening is key.

4. A — Words with the same ending sound
   Rhyming words sound alike at the end.

5. A — Words that make pictures in the mind
   Images are word pictures.

6. B — To know where to stop and breathe
   Pauses help the listener follow.

7. C — They let you practise a word and its meaning again and again
   Flashcards are a simple tool for revision.

8. C — an ending
   Every piece needs an ending.

9. D — To find accurate answers
   Answers should come from the text.

10. A — The order in which things happen
   Sequence means order.

11. B — Say no politely and tell a trusted adult
   Personal safety means not going with strangers.

12. C — Age
   Age records how old you are.

13. A — Reading to learn something new
   We read for information to find facts and learn.

14. A — Taking good care of animals so they are healthy and safe
   Welfare means care for animals' well-being.

15. C — separate items in a list
   Commas separate list items and show short pauses.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: open, read
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

17. (4 marks)
   Answer: I had money, so I bought bread. I wanted a toy, but it was too costly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence and one for each correct comma.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Someone could misuse the details, so a trusted adult should check that it is safe.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the risk, one for asking an adult, one for a clear explanation.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps the reader to understand the message, and it shows respect and builds confidence.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sensible reason.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: strong, big, red, light, new (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each adjective.

21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
